newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms with futures, premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms with futures, premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil was nearly $2 a tonne higher on Friday on the coattails of stronger futures and firm premiums.
May IPE gas oil, which expires midday on Monday, closed $1.75 a tonne higher at $170.75, comfortably breaching earlier strong resistance levels of $170.00.
Traders said activity was still fairly quiet after Thursday's Ascension Day holidays throughout much of continental Europe.
Heating oil barges were heard trading between May IPE +75 cents to May IPE +$1 fob ARA and a diesel cargo was done at May IPE +$11 fob Flushing.

Cargo premiums were also steady with diesel possibly recovering after some mid-week easing. Traders said there was a bid at June IPE +$14 cif Rouen for a small prompt parcel, while larger cargoes were heard offered at June IPE +$12.
A GOM was traded out of the Thames into Spain at June IPE +$15 for May 20-30 dates.
Traders said FOD was pegged unchanged around June IPE +4-5 cif NWE, with DIN about 50-75 cents stronger.
